page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.3xlarge is a compute-focused instance type within the ecs.u0 family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine is configured with 12 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 24.0 GB of memory, which establishes a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage and lacks hardware GPU accelerators. Network baseline bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Hardware resource distribution prioritizes multi-threaded processing capacity over large memory footprints. Because local storage is absent, persistent storage requires external network-attached volumes, decoupling I/O lifecycles from the virtual machine instance. From a resource-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 memory ratio limits unutilized RAM overhead for workloads centered on CPU throughput. Dedicated core allocation prevents shared-core CPU contention across the 12 processing threads.

With its 12-core allocation and 24.0 GB RAM profile, the ecs.u0.c1m2.3xlarge is designed for compute-bound tasks that do not exceed moderate memory thresholds. Suitable use cases include continuous integration agents, build compilation pipelines, batch processing jobs, stateless application serving tiers, and containerized microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.3xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration running on a KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 CPU architecture, it features 12 dedicated vCPUs paired with 24.0 GB of system memory, delivering a 1:2 compute-to-memory balance of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with the hardware profile. This architectural profile provides efficient utilization for workloads that demand parallel thread execution without substantial per-core memory overhead. As a result, the ecs.u0.c1m2.3xlarge is technically aligned with batch compute tasks, continuous integration runners, compilation pipelines, stateless web application servers, and microservice clusters.
